findings.text: follow-on: the two controls are applied together in one run (the mutation header at logs/negative-control.log:3 reads 'mutate both reverted resolutions', and that single run reports 'FF' / '2 failed'), so the docstrings' claim at lines 185 and 226 that each control fails its own case is asserted rather than isolated. A reversion of the access-line path alone reddens only test 1 and a reversion of the bound-check path alone reddens only test 2, and a combined run cannot distinguish which removal caused which failure; the essential guard (reverting the landed mechanism reddens the tests) is still demonstrated, so this does not hold the node.

follow-on: the added _served_log_path(server) sits one letter from the pre-existing _server_log_path() at reckon/serve.py:255, which resolves the same value from the environment on every call and is exactly the resolution this node exists to stop using per request. A future caller reaching for the wrong one gets an environment-resolved path with no error, which is the defect the node repaired; a name that distinguishes the server-object pinning would remove the footgun.

follow-on: the log the manifest's artifacts line names as the head smoke ('logs/head-smoke.log 2 passed in 2.89s EXIT=0') carries a revision header reading '86616aaccec32766944d21a2176dfd7457993c20', the base revision rather than the head, and its tree is a scratch copy (.../_XYZW); the gate that carries the head arm (logs/gate-files-n4.log at 91087a8) is sound, so this is receipt hygiene only, but a reader opening the smoke log to confirm the head run finds a base revision where the head is claimed.
